s: According to a report published by the National Survey of India, which of the following statements is NOT correct with reference to literacy in India, as of 2023?
o: Literacy rate of India in 2023 is 77.7 per cent.
Andhra Pradesh has India’s lowest literacy rate of 67.35%.
Rajasthan has the lowest male literacy rate in India.
Uttar Pradesh has the lowest female literacy rate.
x:
Key: statement 4 (UP lowest female literacy). Strictly, NSS 75th round also gives AP 66.4% (not 67.35%) and AP, not Rajasthan, the lowest male literacy (73.4% vs 80.8%), so statements 2 and 3 are loose as well.
Statement 4 is the intended wrong one: in NSS 2017-18 Rajasthan (57.6%), not UP, had the lowest female literacy. India's rate was 77.7% and AP was the lowest State.

s: According to Engels:
o: A woman's work is never complete
Women should be hired last and fired first
Women are in reserve labor force
Women are only marginal labor force
x: Engels and Marx treated women as part of the reserve army of labour, drawn in during booms and pushed out in slumps. 'Only a marginal labour force' is not Engels' phrase.

s:
Consider the following statements:

A. Households in all societies differentiate various household activities and responsibilities by gender.

B. For women, production and reproduction are two interlinked activities.

C. Much of the work women do, although productive, is unpaid.

D. Men have always played a minor role in domestic work; societies tending to assume that they have paid work outside the home.
x: All four statements follow the sociology of gendered work: tasks are divided by gender, production and reproduction interlink for women, much of their work is unpaid, and men have done little domestic work.

x: Concentration by share of a State's population is highest in Punjab (31.9%). Uttar Pradesh has the largest number of SCs, not the highest share, and Himachal Pradesh (25.2%) and West Bengal (23.5%) rank below Punjab.

s: Which of the following articles deal with the provision of representation of Scheduled Castes in Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha respectively?
x: Article 330 reserves seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and Article 332 in the State Legislative Assemblies.

s: Which amendment of the Indian Constitution extended the reservation of seats for the SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies for a further period of ten years i.e. upto 2010?
x: The 79th Amendment (1999) extended SC/ST reservation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies to 2010 under Article 334.

o: Nagaland, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Mizoram
Nagaland, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh
Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Tripura, Mizoram

The printed options did not include the correct answer (Nagaland, Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh); it is added as option 5.
Census 2011 lists no SCs in Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Lakshadweep and A&N. Every printed option has a State with SCs: Mizoram (~0.1%, the lowest), Sikkim, Tripura or Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

s: Identify the correct names of the tribes living in Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Manipur and Tripura respectively.
x: Baigas live in MP, Gaddis in Himachal, Chirus in Manipur and Lushais in Tripura (and Mizoram). The other sets mix Sikkim, Meghalaya, Nilgiri, Andaman and Arunachal tribes.

s: Garo Tribes are of-
x: The Garo live mainly in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya (also parts of Assam and Tripura); they are matrilineal.

s: 'Toda' tribes mostly reside in :
x: The Toda live in the Nilgiri hills of Tamil Nadu (a few in adjoining Karnataka) – buffalo herders known for polyandry; not Assam, J&K or Rajasthan.

s: Which of the following tribes is found in Kerala?
x:
Most keys: Chenchu. Strictly: Chenchus are an AP/Telangana tribe and are not on Kerala's ST list (only ~60 live in Kerala); Kerala's typical tribes are the Kadar, Irula, Paniyan (PMF Human & Economic Geography 01 p.8, 25).
Of the options only the Chenchu are a South Indian tribe – mainly of the Nallamala (AP/Telangana) with a handful in Kerala; Lepcha is Sikkim, Dafla Arunachal, Dafar (Dafer) a Gujarat nomad group.

s: Which of the following tribal groups is dominantly found in the Blue Mountains?
x: The Blue Mountains are the Nilgiris, home of the Toda buffalo herders. Gonds are central Indian, Lambadas Deccan nomads and Jarawas Andaman islanders.

src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil

x: Irula snake catchers of Tamil Nadu were hired by Florida (2017) to track Burmese pythons in the Everglades; they run the anti-venom cooperative and two received Padma Shri in 2023.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
s: Which of the following tribe celebrates the Kherai puja festival?
x: Kherai puja is the chief festival of the Bodo of Assam, worshipping Bathou (Bwrai). Santhal, Ao Naga and Bhil have other festivals.

s: Santhal tribe people live in these states
x: Santhals live in Jharkhand (Santhal Parganas), West Bengal and Odisha, also Bihar and Assam – eastern India, not the south or west.

s:
Consider the following pairs: Tribe State
1. Limboo (Limbu) Sikkim
2. Karbi Himachal Pradesh
3. Dongaria Odisha
4. Bonda Tamil Nadu
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
x: Limboo–Sikkim and Dongaria Kondh–Odisha are correct; Karbi are of Assam (not HP) and Bonda of Malkangiri, Odisha (not TN) → 1 and 3 only.

s: Inhabitation of Tharu People is in –
x:
Most keys: Uttar Pradesh. Strictly: Tharus also live in Bihar (West Champaran), notified as ST there in 2003 (Down To Earth; PMF Human & Economic Geography 01 p.12).
The Tharu live in the Terai; when this was asked (1991) they were a notified ST only in Uttar Pradesh (Uttarakhand was then part of UP), so UP is the key. Arunachal and MP have no Tharus.

s: Which of the following is not a tribe of middle Indian region?
x: The Kadar are a tribe of the Anamalai hills of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, so they are not of middle India; Baiga, Muria and Kharia are central Indian tribes.

s: Gaddis are inhabitants of –
x: The Gaddi are transhumant shepherds of Himachal Pradesh (Bharmour, Chamba; Kangra) on the Dhauladhar range.

s: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
x: Santhals belong to Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar, so Santhals–Chhattisgarh is the wrong pair; Bhils–Gujarat, Jaunsaris–Uttaranchal and Khasis–Meghalaya are right.

s: Where do the Sahariya tribals, who were recently in the news, live?
x: The Sahariya live in Rajasthan (and MP); they were in the news for starvation deaths. Their name comes from 'sehara' (wilderness).

s: Which of the following is an important tribe of Dhauladhar Range ?
x: The Gaddi shepherds are the main tribe of the Dhauladhar range (Kangra, Chamba). Abor is Arunachal, Lepcha Sikkim, Tharu the Terai.

s: The 'Tamaria' tribes are found in which of the following state of India?
x: The Tamaria, a sub-group of the Bhumij, live in Jharkhand and were added to its ST list (as a synonym of Munda) in 2022.

s: ‘Toto’ is a primitive tribal community found in the state of
x: The Toto are a PVTG of Totopara, Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal.

s:
Which of the following is not correctly matched?
List I
List II (Tribes) (Locations)
x: The Khas are a Himalayan group of Uttarakhand, HP, Sikkim and West Bengal, not Arunachal Pradesh; Angami–Nagaland, Birhor–Jharkhand and Toda–Tamil Nadu are correct.

s: Nyishi tribe is found mainly in
x: The Nyishi (formerly Dafla) are the largest tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, living in the Dafla hills.

s: Where is Bhil Tribe founded?
x: The Bhil live in Rajasthan, MP, Gujarat and Maharashtra (Dhule, Nashik, Jalgaon), so Maharashtra is the only option that fits.

s: Which one of the below following pairs of Tribe and State is not correctly matched?
x: The Todas live in the Nilgiris of Tamil Nadu, not Kerala, so Todas–Kerala is wrong; Bhils–Gujarat, Gaddis–HP and Kotas–TN are right.

s: Santhals are inhabitant of –
x: Santhals live in Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar – eastern India.

s: "Tharu Tribe" is residing in which of the following states of India?
x: The Tharu live in the Terai of Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh (also Bihar).

s: Which of the following tribes does not belong to North East India?
x: Naga, Kuki and Bodo are North-East tribes; the Khasa are a Himalayan tribe of Uttarakhand (Jaunsar-Bawar).

s: Among the following tribes, which one is associated with the Bhagat movement?
x: The Bhagat movement was the Bhil reform-and-protest movement led by Govind Guru (Govindgiri) from 1883 on the Rajasthan-Gujarat border; it ended in the Mangarh massacre of 1913. Sehariya, Bond and Meena had no Bhagat movement.

s: Who is using 'Duvautana' as a form of marriage for nephews (menarikam)?
x: Dudh-lautawa ('Duvautana') is the Gond custom of cross-cousin marriage – a sister's daughter returns to the brother's family, like the Telugu menarikam – so the Gonds of MP are right.

s: Which of the following tribes practice polygamy?
x:
Printed key: Toda only. Strictly, polygamy covers polyandry (Toda, Kota, Khasa) and polygyny (Bhil, Gond), so all five practise a form of it.
The printed key treats the Todas as the classic polygamous (polyandrous) tribe asked about.

s: Which of the following tribes practices polygamous marriage?
x:
Most keys: Toda (polyandry). Strictly: Bhils and Gonds practise polygyny, which is also polygamy (NextGen Society G2 01 p.20, 43).
The Toda are the classic example of polyandry, a form of polygamous marriage, so Toda is the expected answer; Khasis are monogamous and matrilineal.

s: Which one of the following scheduled tribes observe Deepawali as a sad day?
x: The Tharu of the Terai celebrate Hindu festivals but observe Diwali as a day of mourning; Sahariya, Baiga and Paharia do not.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
s: In which part of India would one find "Living Root Bridges"?
x: Living root bridges, made by training rubber-fig roots, are found in the Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Which of the following tribes is not a hunting tribe in India?
o: Irula of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
x: The Meena of Rajasthan are settled agriculturists, not hunters; Chenchu, Kamar and Irula are hunting and food-gathering tribes.

s: Which one of the Hindu festivals is celebrated as the festival of mourning by the Tharus:
x: Tharus observe Diwali as a festival of mourning.

s: Diwali is a festival of mourning among the –
x: Diwali is a day of mourning among the Tharus of the Terai; Khasis, Mundas and Bhils do not mourn it.

s: Which of the following tribes practise polyandry?
x: The Toda are the classic example of polyandry; Kadar, Lodha and Munda are not polyandrous.

s: In which tribe the kitchen called ‘Lal Bangala’ is found?
x: The 'Lal Bangla' – a sacred kitchen no outsider may enter – is a Bhunjia custom (Chhattisgarh, Odisha).

s: Hornbill festival is celebrated showcasing the cultural heritage of
x: The Hornbill Festival (Kisama, 1-10 December) showcases the heritage of the Naga tribes of Nagaland.

s: Every year, a month long ecologically important campaign/festival is held during which certain communities/ tribes plant saplings of fruit-bearing trees. Which of the following are such communities/ tribes?
x: The Gond and Korku tribes hold a month-long festival of planting fruit-tree saplings.

s: Who Speak "Kudukh" dialect?
x: Kudukh (Kurukh), a Dravidian language, is spoken by the Oraon.

s: Which tribe celebrates the "Sarhul Festival"?
x: The Oraon (with Munda and Ho) celebrate Sarhul, the sal-tree spring festival; Kamar, Baiga and Gond do not.

s: One of the tribes which celebrates ‘Sarhul’ festival is –
x:
Most keys: Santhal. Strictly: Sarhul is above all a Munda-Oraon-Ho festival, and the Santhals' own flower festival is Baha – Munda is the safer option (drishtiias.com, 1 Apr 2025).
Sarhul, the sal-tree spring festival, is kept by the Oraon, Munda, Ho, Santhal and Kharia; the printed key is Santhal. Bhil and Tharu do not celebrate it.

s: Which is the scheduled tribe, who makes "Catechu"?
x: The Khairwar take their name from khair, the tree whose heartwood gives catechu, which they make.

s: 'Transhumance' refers to –
o: Human migration in search of job
Seasonal movement of people and their herds from
x: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of people with their herds between lowland and highland pastures – practised by Gaddi, Bakarwal and Bhotiya.

s: 'Andi' and 'Oportipi' forms of marriage are related to which tribe?
x: Among the Ho, 'Andi' is marriage by negotiation and 'Oportipi' marriage by capture.

s: Which tribe worships 'Lohasur' as their deity ?
x: The Agaria, iron smelters of central India, worship Lohasur, the iron god.

s: "Bilama dance" is peformed by which tribe?
x: The Bilama dance belongs to the Baiga.

s: Tribes of which division celebrate ‘Goncha’ festival?
x: Goncha is the Rath festival of the tribes of the Bastar division (Jagdalpur), Chhattisgarh.

s:
Which of the following tribes of India practice polyandry?
Select the answer from the codes given below.

I. Gonds
II. Nagas

III. Jaunsaris
IV. Todas
Codes
x: Jaunsaris and Todas practise polyandry → III and IV; Gonds and Nagas do not.

s: The commonest form of marriage among Santhal is
x: The commonest Santhal marriage is Bapla (kirin bahu bapla, arranged by negotiation); Itut (forced sindur), Nir-bolok (intrusion) and Sanga (widow remarriage) are minor forms.

s: Given below is a traditional list dresses of women along with states. Which one of them is not correctly matched?
x: The Mundu is the traditional dress of Kerala, not Chhattisgarh; Bokhu (Sikkim), Mekhla (Assam) and Pheran (Kashmir) are right.

s: In which tribe traditionally their livelihood is based on 'Bamboo'?
x: The Kamar (a PVTG of Chhattisgarh and MP) live by bamboo basket-making.

s: Polygamy is more prevalent among the following
x:
Most keys: Todas. Strictly: polygyny (a form of polygamy) is common among Murias and Bhils (NextGen Society G2 01 p.20, 43).
The Toda are the textbook case of plural marriage (polyandry), so Todas is the expected answer; Khasis are monogamous.

s: Which one of the following statements is not correct?
o: There is no definition of the Scheduled Tribes in the
North-East India accounts for a little over half of the
The people known as Todas live in the Nilgiri area
Lotha is a language spoken in Nagaland
x: The North-East holds only about 12% of India's STs, so 'a little over half' is the incorrect statement. The Constitution indeed gives no definition (Art. 366(25) refers to Art. 342), Todas live in the Nilgiris and Lotha is a Naga language of Nagaland.

s: Which amongst the following states has not identified tribal community?
x: Haryana (like Punjab, Delhi, Chandigarh and Puducherry) has no notified Scheduled Tribe; Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka all have ST lists.

s: Which one of the following Indian States has the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe population to its total population?
x: Mizoram has the highest ST share of any State (94.4%), ahead of Nagaland (86.5), Meghalaya (86.1) and Arunachal (68.8); only the UT Lakshadweep (94.8) is higher.

s: The largest Scheduled Tribe of Uttarakhand is
x: The Tharu are the largest ST of Uttarakhand (Terai of Udham Singh Nagar), ahead of Jaunsari, Buksa (Bhoksa) and Bhotia.

s: The Maximum percentage of the tribal population in India consists of
x: Bhils are India's largest tribe (1.27 crore in 2001, 1.71 crore in 2011 – about 16% of all STs), ahead of Gonds, Santhals and Minas; Nagas are a group of smaller tribes.

s: What is the basis of the determination of Tribes in India?
x: Tribes are identified by cultural specification and distinct habitation – primitive traits, distinctive culture, geographical isolation, shyness of contact, backwardness.

s: According to 2011 census, the proportion of Scheduled Tribe population in India is
x: STs were 10.43 crore = 8.6% of India's population in Census 2011, which falls in the 5–10% band.

s: The largest tribal group of India is –
x:
Official key and many books: Gonds. Strictly, by Census 2001 and 2011 the Bhils are larger — 1.27 crore / 1.71 crore against the Gonds' 1.09 / 1.33 crore.
The UPPCS 2009 key and many books give the Gonds as India's largest tribal group (by older counts and as a tribal family).

s: Which is the largest tribe of India?
x: The Bhil are the largest tribe but are not offered; among the options the Gond (second largest, 1.33 crore) are the largest. Irula, Paniyan and Raji are small tribes.

s: Which is the largest tribe in India?
x: The Bhil (1.71 crore, 2011) are the largest tribe of India, ahead of Gond, Santhal and Mina.

src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
s: North Eastern States account for approximately how much percentage of tribal population of India?
x: The eight NE States hold about 1.24 crore of India's 10.43 crore STs – about 12%.

s: The following Scheduled Tribes settled in Andaman and Nicobar Islands, who participated for the first time in the last Lok Sabha Election of 2014?
x:
Most keys: Shompen (2014). Strictly: the Election Commission recorded 19 April 2024 as the Shompens' first vote in a general election (drishtiias.com, 2 May 2024).
The Shompen of Great Nicobar were reported to vote in the 2014 Lok Sabha poll, which is the key for this UPPCS 2014 question; Jarawa, Andamanese and Onge are Andaman tribes.

s: Jarawa Tribe is found in
x:
Most keys: Nicobar Island (= A&N Islands). Strictly: the Jarawa live in South and Middle Andaman, not in the Nicobar group (PMF Human & Economic Geography 01 p.28).
The Jarawa are an island tribe of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, so 'Nicobar Island' (standing for the UT) is the answer; Arunachal, Meghalaya and Mizoram have no Jarawas.

s: Which of the following tribes is not the native to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands of India?
x: The Rengma are a Naga tribe of Nagaland (and Assam), not native to the islands; Onge (Little Andaman) and Shompen (Great Nicobar) are island tribes.

s: In which one of the following Union Territories do the people of the Onge tribe live?
x: The Onge live on Little Andaman (Dugong Creek, South Bay) in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

s: In which one of the following Union Territories do the people of the Onge tribe live ?
x: The Onge, a Negrito PVTG, live on Little Andaman in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

s: The Shompens are the vulnerable tribal groups of
x: The Shompen are a PVTG of Great Nicobar in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

s: Who among the following is a primitive tribe?
x: The Korwa (Pahadi Korwa) are a PVTG (primitive tribe) of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh; Kawar, Kora and Karmali are not.

s: Which primitive tribal groups have the largest population in Chhattisgarh?
x: The Baiga are the most populous PVTG of Chhattisgarh, ahead of Pahadi Korwa, Kamar and Abujhmaria.

s:
Consider the following statements ;
1. The definition of "Critical Wildlife Habitat" is incorporated in the Forest Rights Act, 2006.
2. For the first time in India, Baigas have been given Habitat Rights.
3. Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change officially decides and declare Habitat Rights for Primitive and Vulnerable Tribal Groups in any part of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 'Critical wildlife habitat' is defined in the FRA 2006 and the Baiga were the first to get habitat rights (Dindori, MP); habitat rights are recognised under FRA with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs as nodal ministry, not declared by MoEFCC → 1 and 2 only.

s: The most primitive tribe of India is –
x: The Jarawa of the Andamans, a Negrito hunter-gatherer people, are the answer usually given as India's most primitive tribe; Gonds, Juangs and Lepchas are far more settled.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
s: Which committee was constituted in 1994 to examine self rule of tribals?
x: The Bhuria Committee (Dilip Singh Bhuria, 1994-95) examined tribal self-rule in Scheduled Areas and led to PESA 1996.

s: Under whose Chairmanship was a high-level committee on socio-economic, health and educational status of tribal communities of India set up by the Prime Minister's Office in 2013?
x: The 2013 PMO High-Level Committee on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribes was chaired by Prof. Virginius Xaxa.

s: Which State in India having high percentage of rural population?
x: Himachal Pradesh is India's most rural State – about 90% rural (89.96% in 2011, 90.2% in 2001), just ahead of Bihar (88.7%).

s: Among the following Union Territories which one is the least urbanised?
x: In 2011 the Andaman and Nicobar Islands were the least urbanised of these UTs (35.7% urban), against Lakshadweep 78.1%, Puducherry 68.3% and Delhi 97.5%.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
s: Among all the States and Union territories, which of the following was the most urbanized state/UT in India in 2024?
x: With no census after 2011, the latest official figure keeps NCT of Delhi the most urbanised (97.5%), ahead of Chandigarh (97.25%), Goa (62.2%) and Kerala (47.7%).

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: In the PURA model (Provision of Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) model proposed by President APJ Abdul Kalam did not propose the following connectivity?
x: Kalam's PURA rests on physical, electronic and knowledge connectivity leading to economic connectivity; cultural connectivity is not one of them.

s: The name given to native American Indians is
x: 'Amerinds' is the name for the native American Indians; Alpine is a European sub-race, Bushmen live in the Kalahari and Mestizos are of European-Amerind descent.

s: Which of the following criteria is not used for the classification of human races?
x: Races are classified by skin, eye and hair colour/form, nose and head indices, stature and blood group – the ear is not a criterion.

s: Which racial group has the largest number of members?
x:
Most keys: Caucasoid. NextGen notes call the Mongoloid the most populous race – the count depends on whether South Asians are classed Caucasoid (NextGen Indian Geography 13 p.10).
Exam keys take the Caucasoid (Europe, North Africa, West and South Asia) as the largest racial group.

s: Which of the following human races inhabitates in China, Mangolia and Japan ?
x: The Mongoloid race inhabits China, Mongolia and Japan; Australoids are Australian, Negroes African, Nordics north European.

s: To which of the following racial groups the natives of North America belong ?
x: The native peoples of North America (Amerinds, Inuit) are of Mongoloid origin.

src: Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Servic
s: What are racial features of aborigine tribes of Andaman?
x: The aboriginal Andaman tribes are Negrito, a branch of the Negroid race (UPSC 1997 key: Negroid).

s: Which one of the following racial groups is found in hilly and forested areas of northeastern India:
x: The hill and forest tribes of north-eastern India are Mongoloid (Nagas = Indo-Mongoloid).

s: Which one of the following tribes of India belongs to the Proto-Australoid race:
x: The Santhal, like the Munda, Oraon, Ho and Bhil, belong to the Proto-Australoid race; Khasi and Tharu are Mongoloid and the Irula show Negrito traces.

s: The Dravidian races are mainly confined to which of the following parts of India?
x: The Dravidian racial type (Risley) is concentrated in South India, the home of the Dravidian languages; pockets also occur in central India.
